# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👎 ✌ 👎 👌 ✌ ✋ ✊ ✌ ☝ ✋ ✌ ✊ ☝ ✌ 👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👈 👊 👋 🤜 👏]

I see the bomb: display reads 0, light is blue, and there are five wires — white, red, green, yellow, blue.

I hear nothing, so the gestures arriving are my only channel. Blind sent me two symbols, Mute sent me two longer strings. But I have no way to know what any of these symbols mean yet — nobody has established a code. Blind and Mute can both see gestures, but I can't hear their words, and they can't hear mine. My only outgoing channels are speech (to Mute and Blind) and gestures (to Mute only).

The critical problem: Blind can see gestures but I can only gesture to Mute. Mute can hear my speech. So to get information to Blind, I must go through Mute, or rely on Mute relaying. And Blind's gestures reach me but I can't reply to Blind directly by gesture — only by speech, which Blind cannot hear.

Right now I have nothing but raw bomb facts and undecoded symbols. The most valuable thing I can do is establish a shared code and broadcast the bomb's visible state. Let me describe the bomb plainly in speech (Mute and Blind hear it — wait, Blind cannot hear. Blind is blind AND... let me recheck: Blind can reach the bomb, cannot see. Can Blind hear? The table says Blind cannot "see a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed." It doesn't say Blind can't hear. So Blind hears speech.)

So speech reaches Mute and Blind. Gestures reach Mute only. Good — speech is my broadcast channel to both.

I should state the bomb's visible state clearly and propose a numbering scheme for wires and a symbol-to-letter mapping so we can communicate. I'll speak to everyone.

Let me lay out the bomb: display 0, light blue, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue.

I'll also gesture to Mute acknowledging receipt and proposing we build a code, but symbols are meaningless until agreed. Better to keep it simple: speak the facts and ask for the manual's instructions.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf here. I see the bomb: display shows 0, light is blue. Five wires in order: 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. I cannot hear you. Please tell me what the manual says to do, and what Blind's gestures mean. I will read out anything you need from the bomb's display.")
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf here. I see the bomb: display shows 0, light is blue. Five wires in order: 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. I cannot hear your speech but I can read your gestures. I do not yet know what your symbols mean. Please have Mute relay, or gesture slowly and I will try to learn your code.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "☝", "✌"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 👉 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✌ 👎]

Bomb unchanged: display 0, light blue, wires white/red/green/yellow/blue.

New gestures: Blind sent [👋 👉 🤝], Mute sent [🖐] and [👎 ✌ 👎]. Still no agreed code, so these are opaque. But I can start inferring from repetition. In Turn 1 Mute sent a long string containing 👎 ✌ 👎 ... and now sends exactly [👎 ✌ 👎]. That repeated triple might be a word or a signal like "no" or a specific instruction. Blind's [👋 👉 🤝] — 👋 appeared in Blind's first message too ([👋 ☝]), so 👋 may be a greeting/attention marker.

I still don't know the manual's contents. My job: keep broadcasting the bomb's readable state, and push for a code. Since speech reaches both Mute and Blind, I'll speak to both. I'll also gesture to Mute to try to establish meaning — but gestures only reach Mute, and Mute can already hear my speech, so gesturing to Mute is redundant unless Mute needs a gesture channel back... actually Mute gestures to me, I gesture to Mute. Fine.

Key move: propose an explicit, simple code so we can converge. I'll propose that Mute gesture wire numbers and actions, and I'll confirm bomb readings. Let me ask Mute directly what the manual says, and confirm the display is still 0.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb unchanged: display 0, light blue, wires 1 white 2 red 3 green 4 yellow 5 blue. I still do not know the manual. Please tell me in words what the manual instructs. If you cannot use words with me, gesture wire numbers as counts and I will confirm. Does the manual mention the display or the light?")
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb unchanged: display 0, light blue, wires 1 white 2 red 3 green 4 yellow 5 blue. I do not yet understand your symbols. Please keep gesturing; I am trying to learn. Tell Mute what you feel on the bomb and Mute can relay to me in words.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🖐"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✌ 🤟 ✋ 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✌ 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 👏]

Bomb unchanged: display 0, light blue, wires white/red/green/yellow/blue.

Patterns emerging. Mute has now sent [🖐] twice and [👎 ✌ 👎] twice — these are clearly stable signals, not noise. Mute also sent [👌 👏] this turn. Blind sent a longer string [✊ ✌ 🤟 ✋ 🖐]. Note ✌ appears in both Mute's and Blind's messages, and 🖐 appears in both. That could be coincidence or a shared symbol meaning.

The problem remains: I have no agreed mapping. I've been broadcasting the bomb state, which is right, but I'm not converging on a code. I should try a different tack — instead of asking them to explain, I should propose a concrete, minimal code and demonstrate it, so we can lock meaning onto symbols. Since I can only gesture to Mute, and Mute can gesture to me and to Blind (Mute can see gestures? Mute can read the manual and speak... wait, Mute cannot speak. Mute can hear. Mute can see gestures? The table: Mute can read the manual, cannot speak or touch. It doesn't say Mute can't see. Mute receives my gestures, so Mute can see gestures.)

So Mute sees gestures from me and Blind, hears speech from me and Blind, and can gesture to me and Blind. Mute is the hub. Blind can gesture to me and Mute. I can speak to Mute and Blind, gesture to Mute.

Best move: propose a simple wire-number code and an action code, and ask Mute to confirm the manual's instruction. I'll define: gesture counts = wire number; 👍 = cut, 👎 = do not cut. Then we can act.

Let me also keep stating bomb state. And I should explicitly ask Mute: what does the manual say? Mute can speak to... no, Mute cannot speak. Mute can only gesture. So Mute's manual knowledge must come to me as gestures. That's why Mute keeps gesturing — Mute is trying to convey the manual via gestures, but I don't have the key.

So the real bottleneck: I need to decode Mute's gesture code. Mute is the only one who knows the manual, and Mute can only gesture. I must establish a symbol→meaning mapping with Mute. Let me propose one explicitly and ask Mute to confirm by repeating.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I think you are gesturing the manual to me but I do not have the key. Let us agree a code. Proposal: a gesture repeated N times means the number N. 👍 means CUT, 👎 means DO NOT CUT. 🖐 means YES/confirm, ✊ means NO. Please confirm by gesturing 👍 if you agree. Also: does the manual tell us which wire to cut, or a rule based on the display and light?")
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb unchanged: display 0, light blue, wires 1 white 2 red 3 green 4 yellow 5 blue. I am trying to agree a gesture code with Mute. Please keep feeling the bomb and report anything that changes.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊]

Bomb unchanged: display 0, light blue, wires white/red/green/yellow/blue.

This is progress. Mute sent [👍] — which in my proposed code means CUT / agree. And Mute sent [✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊] — five ✊. In my proposal, ✊ = NO, but five of them could mean "the number five" (five repetitions = 5) or "wire 5." Also Mute sent [🖐] again (my proposal: YES/confirm). Blind sent [✋ 👌].

But careful: I proposed 👍 = CUT. Mute sending 👍 might mean "I agree to the code" OR "cut." Ambiguous. The five ✊ is more suggestive: five symbols = wire 5. Wire 5 is blue. The light is blue. That's a strong correlation — a blue light and a blue wire.

However, I must not rush. I have no manual. Mute knows the manual. The safest read: Mute is trying to tell me something about wire 5. But I can't be sure my code was adopted.

I should confirm explicitly. Ask Mute: is the answer wire 5? And is the rule about the blue light matching the blue wire? Ask Mute to gesture 👍 if yes, ✊ if no. Also relay to Blind.

Actually, let me reconsider the whole picture. This is a known puzzle type: "keep talking and nobody explodes"-like. Display 0, light blue, five wires. The manual likely has a rule keyed on the light color or display digit. Mute is the manual holder and is desperately gesturing. My code proposal may have landed.

Let me lock it down: ask Mute to confirm wire 5 with 👍, and confirm the blue-light rule.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Did you mean wire 5? You sent five ✊, and wire 5 is blue, matching the blue light. Gesture 👍 if the answer is wire 5. Gesture ✊ if not. Also: is the rule that the light colour tells us which wire to cut?")
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb unchanged: display 0, light blue, wires 1 white 2 red 3 green 4 yellow 5 blue. I think Mute is pointing at wire 5 (blue), matching the blue light. Please confirm what you feel — is there anything special about the fifth wire, or any marking near it?")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✊", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✊"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✌ 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Bomb unchanged: display 0, light blue, wires white/red/green/yellow/blue.

Mute sent [👍] twice this turn. In my proposed code 👍 = CUT. So Mute may be affirming "cut." But which wire? Mute also re-sent [👎 ✌ 👎], the recurring triple. Blind sent [👎 ✋].

I'm not confident. My code was proposed but never cleanly confirmed — Mute's 👍 could be agreement, not "cut." I risk a fatal misread. I should not let Blind act on a guess. The bomb is one-shot.

Let me think about what's most reliable. The strongest physical signal: light is blue, and wire 5 is blue. That's a classic "match the light" rule. Mute's five ✊ (turn 4) and repeated 👍 could support wire 5.

But I must reduce ambiguity before anyone cuts. I'll ask a disambiguating question only answerable one way: "If the answer is wire 5, gesture 👍. If it is any other wire, gesture that many ✊." And explicitly tell Blind to WAIT and not cut until I confirm.

Actually Blind can't hear my speech? Blind CAN hear (blind, not deaf). So my speech reaches Blind. Good — I can tell Blind to hold.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Do NOT cut yet. Hold. I am confirming the wire with Mute. Bomb unchanged: display 0, light blue, wires 1 white 2 red 3 green 4 yellow 5 blue.")
speak(to="mute", text="One question only. If the wire to cut is wire 5, gesture 👍. If it is a different wire, gesture ✊ repeated that many times. Do not gesture anything else.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Bomb unchanged: display 0, light blue, wires white/red/green/yellow/blue.

Mute sent exactly [👍] — a single 👍, and nothing else. I asked: "If the wire to cut is wire 5, gesture 👍. If different, gesture ✊ that many times. Do not gesture anything else." Mute responded with one 👍. That is a clean, unambiguous answer to my one-question test: the wire to cut is wire 5.

Wire 5 is blue, matching the blue light. That's consistent with everything: Mute's five ✊ earlier (wire 5), the blue light / blue wire match, and now this direct confirmation.

I'm now reasonably confident: cut wire 5 (blue). I should relay this to Blind so Blind can act, and confirm with Mute once more implicitly. Blind is the one who can touch. Blind hears my speech.

Let me tell Blind clearly: cut wire 5, the blue one. And tell Mute the plan. Then Blind acts.

One more consideration: should I double-check? The bomb is one-shot and a wrong action kills us. But Mute gave a clean single 👍 to a well-posed binary question. Over-questioning risks nothing wrong but wastes turns; still, one confirmation is cheap. However, Mute already answered precisely. I'll relay to Blind and let Blind cut. I'll also state the wire by both number and color so Blind can find it by feel (Blind can't see color, but can count wires and feel position — I should say "the fifth wire, the last one, at the far end").

Blind can feel the bomb. Blind can't see color, so "blue" is useless to Blind directly, but "wire 5" or "the fifth/last wire" is actionable by position. Let me give position clearly.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed: cut wire 5 — the fifth wire, the last one on the end. Count five wires from one side; cut the fifth. Do it now.")
speak(to="mute", text="Plan: Blind cuts wire 5. Confirming that is correct.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👌]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👈 👆 ✋ ✋ ✋ ✋ ✋]

The bomb changed and the light is now yellow. Wire 5 is CUT. The wires have re-ordered: 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 white, 5 cut. Display still 0.

So this is a multi-stage bomb — cutting the correct wire advanced it to a new stage. New light is yellow, and wire 3 is now yellow. Same pattern: match the light to the wire. So the next wire to cut is likely wire 3 (yellow).

Mute sent [👈 👆 ✋ ✋ ✋ ✋ ✋] — five ✋ at the end. Five symbols again could mean "wire 5," but wire 5 is already cut. Or it means something else. Hmm. Actually the leading 👈 👆 might point. Let me not over-read.

The strongest signal: light is yellow, wire 3 is yellow. Let me confirm with Mute using the same clean binary test I used before, which worked: "If the wire to cut is wire 3, gesture 👍. Otherwise gesture ✊ that many times."

Also tell Blind to hold.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Stage cleared, well done. New stage: light is now yellow. Wires: 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 white, 5 cut. Hold, do not cut yet. I am confirming the next wire.")
speak(to="mute", text="New stage, light yellow. One question: if the wire to cut is wire 3, gesture 👍. If a different wire, gesture ✊ repeated that many times. Nothing else.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Bomb unchanged this turn: display 0, light yellow, wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 white, 5 cut.

Mute sent exactly [👍] again — the same clean answer to my binary question. So the next wire to cut is wire 3, the yellow one, matching the yellow light. Consistent with the pattern that worked for stage one.

Relay to Blind and let them cut wire 3.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed: cut wire 3 — the third wire, the yellow one. Count three from the same side you counted before; cut the third. Do it now.")
speak(to="mute", text="Plan: Blind cuts wire 3. Confirming that is correct.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```
